Residuals from a brsmm model

Source: R/brsmm-methods.R
residuals.brsmm.Rd

Residuals of a "brsmm" fit. The types of residuals.brs are evaluated at the conditional modes of the random effects (ranef.brsmm); for "rqr" and "cell_deviance", re selects how the random effects enter.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'brsmm'
residuals(
  object,
  type = c("response", "pearson", "deviance", "rqr", "weighted", "sweighted",
    "cell_deviance"),
  re = c("conditional", "marginal", "posterior"),
  n_draws = 200L,
  ...
)

Arguments

object

A fitted "brsmm" object.

type

Character: "response" (default), "pearson", "deviance", "rqr", "weighted", "sweighted" or "cell_deviance" (see residuals.brs).

re

"conditional" (default), "marginal" or "posterior"; for type = "rqr" and "cell_deviance" only (see Details).

n_draws

Number of importance-sampling proposals per group for re = "posterior" (default 200; 1 keeps the Gaussian draw).

...

Currently ignored.

Value

Numeric vector, one value per observation.

Details

re applies to type = "rqr" and "cell_deviance":

"conditional"

(default) at the conditional modes \(\hat b_g\). The modes are shrunk toward zero, so the "rqr" residuals are not exactly \(N(0, 1)\) under the model; the shrinkage is strongest for small groups.

"marginal"

from the marginal (population-averaged) distribution of each observation, with the random effects integrated out: \(v_i \sim U(F_m(l_i), F_m(u_i))\), \(F_m(y) = \int F(y \mid b)\, \varphi(b; 0, \hat D)\, db\), computed on the quadrature rule of brs_marginal (for score data \(F_m(l_i)\) and \(F_m(u_i)\) are the marginal cdf of the score at \(s_i - 1\) and \(s_i\)). The rule integrates \(z = u/\mathrm{SD}(u)\) over \([-8.5, 8.5]\), so marginal probabilities below about \(10^{-15}\) are approximate (this matters for "cell_deviance" in extreme tails only). Each "rqr" residual is \(N(0, 1)\) under the model; residuals of the same group are correlated, since they share the group's random effects.

"posterior"

at one draw of each \(b_g\) from its posterior given the group's data, by sampling-importance-resampling: n_draws proposals from \(N(\hat b_g, H_g^{-1})\) (\(H_g\), the curvature of the log posterior at the mode, by central differences; the prior \(N(0, \hat D)\) shape when it is not positive definite) weighted by posterior over proposal density, and one of them kept. At the true parameters, \((b_g, y_g)\) with \(b_g\) drawn from its posterior has the joint law of the model, so the "rqr" residuals are independent \(N(0, 1)\) (up to the resampling approximation, of order 1/n_draws) without the shrinkage of the modes; at the estimates this holds approximately. Unlike the marginal residuals, the residuals of a group are then nearly independent.

"rqr" residuals use \(v_i\) uniform on \((F(l_i), F(u_i))\) (survival scale above the median, to keep the precision of upper-tail cells), kept in \([10^{-10}, 1 - 10^{-10}]\). "cell_deviance" residuals are \(\mathrm{sign}_i \sqrt{-2 \log P_i}\) with the conditional, marginal or posterior-draw cell probability \(P_i\) and expected score \(\sum_s s P(S = s) / \sum_s P(S = s)\), as in residuals.brs. The "rqr" residuals and the "posterior" draws are random: set a seed to reproduce them.

See also

brsmm, fitted.brsmm, plot.brsmm, residuals.brs

Examples

# \donttest{
dat <- data.frame(
  y = c(
    0, 5, 20, 50, 75, 90, 100, 30, 60, 45,
    10, 40, 55, 70, 85, 25, 35, 65, 80, 15
  ),
  x1 = rep(c(1, 2), 10),
  id = factor(rep(1:4, each = 5))
)
prep <- brs_prep(dat, ncuts = 100)
#> brs_prep: n = 20 | exact = 0, left = 1, right = 1, interval = 18
fit <- brsmm(y ~ x1, random = ~ 1 | id, data = prep)
head(residuals(fit))
#> [1] -0.3855953 -0.2593261 -0.1856053  0.1906739  0.3643947  0.3286716
head(residuals(fit, type = "pearson"))
#> [1] -1.3225376 -0.9366406 -0.6366000  0.6886809  1.2498228  1.1087368
# }
# Quantile residuals without the shrinkage of the conditional modes
d <- expand.grid(visit = 1:5, id = 1:60)
set.seed(3)
s <- brsmm_sim(~ visit, random = ~ 1 | id, data = d, beta = c(-0.6, 0.1),
               phi = qlogis(0.2), re_sd = 0.7, ncuts = 10)
m <- brsmm(y ~ visit, random = ~ 1 | id, data = s)
set.seed(1)
r_m <- residuals(m, type = "rqr", re = "marginal")
r_p <- residuals(m, type = "rqr", re = "posterior")
round(c(mean_m = mean(r_m), sd_m = sd(r_m), mean_p = mean(r_p), sd_p = sd(r_p)), 2)
#> mean_m   sd_m mean_p   sd_p 
#>   0.01   1.00  -0.01   1.00
